messages:
maya: Heads up — after the midnight merge I see decode p95 jump ~18% on the small-batch chat benchmark. Not universal, but consistent on short-seq workloads.

sam: ugh. which merge? any suspect commit/PR?

maya: PR #4821 (fused-attn-warmup) + a follow-up hotpatch in 4823 that tweaked the batcher steering.

sam: OK. I repro locally with canary profile. Short sequence (len<=32) runs slower; long seqs look unchanged. KV eviction count also increased ~2x in the traces.

leo: CI perf bot just flagged this too: @ci-bot any details?

ci-bot: CI perf check: canary-decode-e2e baseline=48ms p95 -> current=58ms p95 (+21%). Test: small-batch-chat-fast. Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/perf/1732109876/

anya: putting rollout on hold for the deduped fleet. Can we get a flamegraph?

sam: ran a quick `pprof` dump from the canary instance. Key diff: attention kernel path switched from `attn_dispatch_v2` -> `attn_fused_matmul_v3` for 12-head models when microbatch==1. The fused kernel has higher overhead on short sequences: warmup + memcopy for KV. Snippet:```
Top 10 functions by cpu
attn_fused_matmul_v3  56.3%  (was 11.8%)
kv_cache_evict         12.1%  (was 3.4%)
decode_loop            8.9%   (was 15.2%)
```

leo: that matches my perf traces — the kernel selector heuristic bumped fused kernel for throughput reasons but it doesn't pay off for short-seq single-turn chat. Also the steering logic increased prefetch concurrency which seems to nudge kv eviction.

maya: interesting — the merge changed two things: 1) selector threshold moved from 32->24 tokens for fused path; 2) batcher steering now tries to combine single-turn requests into microbatch of 2 with aggressive latency budget. Both could explain it.

rafael: can we confirm by forcing the older kernel in the canary? e.g., env `FORCE_KERNEL=attn_dispatch_v2` and run the same workload.

sam: did that: with FORCE_KERNEL v2 p95 back down to 49ms and kv evictions drop to baseline. So kernel choice is the main culprit. Batcher change contributes but smaller.

anya: sounds like a revert + follow-up to adjust selector heuristics. Who can draft the revert?

maya: I'll open a revert PR for the selector change (revert commit 6a7f2d0). We'll hold the rolling canary.

leo: one more ask — add a regression test in perf CI that pins short-seq microbatch=1 and runs with both kernels to catch swaps. Right now CI only checks longform throughput.

sam: good call. I'll add a small-batch p95 test and a quick `pprof` smoke to assert that fused kernel doesn't exceed 1.2x baseline on len<=32.

ci-bot: Perf test ticket created: PERF-724. CI will re-run once PR is up.

maya: plan: (1) revert kernel-selector tweak (PR in 30m), (2) add CI short-seq smoke (sam), (3) evaluate batcher steering separately and open a tuning PR (rafael).

rafael: I'll take the batcher tuning. My suspicion: the steering's aggressiveness threshold is too low and it triggers microbatching in low-load bursts, increasing KV churn. I'll add metrics: per-request `kv_evict_count` and `microbatch_merge_rate`.

sam: note for the postmortem: include flamegraphs, pprof diffs, kernel-selection logs, and the exact commit SHAs. Also record that fused kernel perf regressions are workload-dependent — important for rollout policies.

maya: OK rolling hold in the console and pinging customers on the deduped plan. Thanks team — will update thread with PR link and CI run ID.

ci-bot: Canary hold applied by @anya at 2024-11-12T03:05:12Z.
